string-array.name: tutorial_instructions
string-array.item: Connect start 0 to extraction 6 using dominoes. Practice is independent: it does not spend credits or change records.
Select the highlighted 0–2 tile. Each tile occupies two cells.
Tap the highlighted cell beside start. ALL external touching values must match; the two halves within a tile may differ.
Valid connection! Place one tile per turn. Occupied cells and firewalls cannot hold new tiles.
Select 2–0. We need its 0 next to start.
Press Rotate: the tile is now vertical.
Press Rotate again: it is horizontal with reversed halves. Four rotations restore the original position.
Place the tile in the highlighted cell. Its 0 now matches start.
Execute turn. You must first place a tile. Trace increases by 8 plus pending script noise.
A tile is drawn if the bag has any, RAM recovers to 3 and a script may be drawn. Noise resets; accumulated trace does not.
Firewalls block cells. The daemon threatens start as it moves through the network. Traps are hidden; visible bonuses give RAM or reduce trace.
Select 0–2 to explore the two cells beside start.
Place the highlighted tile to collect RAM and cooling. This exercise also has a hidden trap.
The trap adds 20 noise and discards a script. Execute turn to see trace accumulate.
Watch trace and the daemon each turn. Cooling removes 8 trace; a reserve gives 1 RAM, capped at 3.
Press PING. It costs 1 RAM, adds no noise, previews the next tile and reveals one hidden trap if present.
Observe the revealed trap. PING does not remove traps or change the bag. Collect the RAM from the tile, then use KILL before ending this turn.
Select SPOOF. On confirmation it costs 2 RAM and adds 5 noise. It changes one half of a tile to a value from 0 to 6.
Select the 1–2 tile to modify.
Choose its second half.
Choose value 3. No resources have been spent yet.
Press Cancel. The tile and resources remain unchanged.
Select SPOOF again to make a useful change.
Select the 1–2 tile.
Choose the first half, which contains 1.
Choose 0 so it can connect to start.
Press Apply. RAM is spent, noise is added and the tile changes.
Select the modified 0–2 tile.
Place it beside start. SPOOF helps when no value matches.

Select KILL PROCESS. It costs 3 RAM and adds 15 noise. It removes a firewall, visible honeypot or a complete placed domino when you tap either half. PING discoveries can be removed in the same turn with enough RAM. It cannot remove the daemon.
Tap the highlighted firewall. Any bridge on it is also removed.
Select 0–2: the blocked cell is now free.
Place the tile in the highlighted cell.
Select BRIDGE. It costs 2 RAM and adds 10 noise. It joins the ends of a firewall without removing it and requires an adjacent tile.
Switch the bridge to horizontal: our connection runs left to right.
The bridge is now horizontal and ready to connect the firewall.
Tap the highlighted firewall. This bridge transmits value 2. If both ends are occupied, their values must match.
Select 2–6 to continue on the other side.
Place it in the highlighted cell. Tiles do not occupy the firewall.
Select 4–6 to complete the route.
Place the highlighted tile: 4 continues the network and 6 touches extraction.
Execute turn to check victory. Connecting is not enough: keep trace below 100 and prevent the daemon reaching start during turn resolution.
Victory! You can also lose by exceeding challenge limits, exhausting tiles before reaching extraction, or having neither a legal move nor a rescue script.
Outside practice, victory earns 20 credits and the first win in each challenge adds 40. Every 5 completed challenges unlock a scenario. Skins are cosmetic; free play generates a random board.
Select the 0–2 tile after PING.
Place it beside start to collect the RAM reserve.
Select KILL PROCESS in the same turn. It costs 3 RAM and adds 15 noise.
Tap the revealed honeypot to destroy it before ending the turn.
Execute the turn after both scripts have resolved.
